newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak NBS,banks agree on new money market volumes.
newsitem.headline: Slovak NBS,banks agree on new money market volumes.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) and the eight reference banks on the money market on Tuesday agreed to lower their minimum required volumes in the face of a liquidity drought.

"Some of the banks demanded the end of quoting longer maturities but in the end we accepted a compromise proposal to lower the compulsory quoted volumes by one half for one month starting on Wednesday," said Martin Hrozany, chief dealer at Slovenska Sporitelna.

Reference banks must provide bid/offer quotations for standard deposit maturities, with a set spread, and must have certain minimum credit lines as well as minimum trading volumes for other market participants.
Quotations from the eight banks are used to determine the Bratislava Interbank Offered Rate (BRIBOR).
Under the agreement, Hrozany said maturities of two and three months will now have a minimum volume of 50 million crowns, while four to six month terms will have a 25 million crown minimum volume.
Rates from three to six months are most commonly used to determine the instruments such as swaps and forwards.
"All of this is due to worries of interest rate losses and the instability caused by the current illiquidity of the market. All banks agreed with this proposal," he added.

The market has faced an acute liquidity shortage, according to dealers, since the NBS stopped quoting securities repo and reverse repo rates, opting instead to hold tenders on a daily basis, if needed, for limited volumes of short-term securities repurchases.
The NBS said that by reducing the refinancing volumes, it hoped to help curb credit expansion which is at the heart of the growing money supply.

Peter Andresic, head of NBS Open Market Operations, said after the meeting that the reference banks "challenged the central bank to reassess some matters which could contribute to the market's stabilisation".
"All I can say is that I will pass this message on to central bank officials," he added.

Slovak interbank money market rates steadied at 26.4 percent for overnight funds on Tuesday, with dealers saying the banking sector was in a liquidity crunch ahead of Wednesday's minimum reserve deadline.
The current overnight rate level is equal to the penalty of three times the discount rate, which banks must pay if they fail to meet minimum reserve demands.
